review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

6:1.sourceText: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ἐπιμένωμεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσῃ;
6:1.targetText: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:2.sourceText: μὴ γένοιτο. οἵτινες ἀπεθάνομεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, πῶς ἔτι ζήσομεν ἐν αὐτῇ;
6:2.targetText: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?

groups.note: μὴ γένοιτο ("may it never be") is the fixed formula of rejection, rendered Certainly not.
The future ζήσομεν ("shall we live") is rendered can we … live.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:3.sourceText: ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν, εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν;
6:3.targetText: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?

groups.note: ἀγνοεῖτε ("are you ignorant") is rendered aren’t you aware; there is no separate Greek negative.
ὅσοι ("as many as") is rendered all of … who.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:4.sourceText: συνετάφημεν οὖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Πατρός, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν.
6:4.targetText: We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves οὕτως ("so"), which answers just as, untranslated.

6:5.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐσόμεθα·
6:5.targetText: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.

groups.note: σύμφυτοι ("united") is understood again in the second clause, and BSB repeats it.
ὁμοιώματι ("likeness") is rendered like.
The genitive θανάτου ("of death") is rendered in … death.
ἀλλά opening the conclusion of the if-sentence is rendered certainly.
The article τῆς is rendered as the possessive His.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the one we are united with; the Greek has no pronoun here.
English adds a demonstrative pointing back to burial through baptism (6:4); the Greek has none.
English supplies the one we are united with; the Greek has no pronoun here.

6:6.sourceText: τοῦτο γινώσκοντες, ὅτι ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνεσταυρώθη, ἵνα καταργηθῇ τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τοῦ μηκέτι δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ·
6:6.targetText: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.

groups.note: The articular infinitive τοῦ δουλεύειν ("to serve as slaves") is rendered that … should be slaves.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τοῦτο ("this"), which points ahead to the that-clause, untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle γινώσκοντες ("knowing").
English supplies the one crucified with; the Greek has no pronoun here.

6:7.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν δεδικαίωται ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας.
6:7.targetText: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἀποθανών ("having died") is rendered anyone who has died.
δεδικαίωται ("has been justified") with ἀπό is rendered has been freed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:8.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ἀπεθάνομεν σὺν Χριστῷ, πιστεύομεν ὅτι καὶ συνζήσομεν αὐτῷ,
6:8.targetText: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.

groups.note: Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

6:9.sourceText: εἰδότες ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὐκέτι ἀποθνῄσκει, θάνατος αὐτοῦ οὐκέτι κυριεύει.
6:9.targetText: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.

groups.note: The participle εἰδότες ("knowing") gives the reason, rendered For … know.
The participle ἐγερθείς ("having been raised") is rendered since … was raised.
οὐκέτι ("no longer") is rendered cannot … again.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle εἰδότες ("knowing").

6:10.sourceText: ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν, τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ· ὃ δὲ ζῇ, ζῇ τῷ Θεῷ.
6:10.targetText: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.

groups.note: The relative ὅ ("what") is rendered The death.
The relative ὅ ("what") is rendered the life.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:11.sourceText: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς λογίζεσθε ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι νεκροὺς μὲν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ζῶντας δὲ τῷ Θεῷ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
6:11.targetText: So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the infinitive εἶναι ("to be") untranslated after count.
BSB leaves μέν untranslated; the δέ that answers it is rendered but.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:12.sourceText: Μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις αὐτοῦ,
6:12.targetText: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.

groups.note: εἰς τό with the infinitive is rendered so that.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the infinitive ὑπακούειν ("to obey").

6:13.sourceText: μηδὲ παριστάνετε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα ἀδικίας τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἀλλὰ παραστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς τῷ Θεῷ ὡσεὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ζῶντας καὶ τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ Θεῷ,
6:13.targetText: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.

groups.note: μηδέ ("and not") is rendered not.
μέλη ("members") is rendered parts of … body.
The imperative παραστήσατε also governs the second object, and BSB repeats it.
νεκρῶν ("the dead") is rendered death.
The participle ζῶντας ("living") is rendered those who … to life.
Θεῷ ("God") is rendered Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb for the passage from death to life.

6:14.sourceText: ἁμαρτία γὰρ ὑμῶν οὐ κυριεύσει· οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν.
6:14.targetText: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.

groups.note: κυριεύσει ("will rule over") is rendered shall be … master.

6:15.sourceText: Τί οὖν; ἁμαρτήσωμεν ὅτι οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν; μὴ γένοιτο.
6:15.targetText: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!

groups.note: μὴ γένοιτο ("may it never be") is the fixed formula of rejection, rendered Certainly not.

6:16.sourceText: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ᾧ παριστάνετε ἑαυτοὺς δούλους εἰς ὑπακοήν, δοῦλοί ἐστε ᾧ ὑπακούετε, ἤτοι ἁμαρτίας εἰς θάνατον ἢ ὑπακοῆς εἰς δικαιοσύνην;
6:16.targetText: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?

groups.note: εἰς ὑπακοήν ("for obedience") is rendered obedient.
δοῦλοι is understood again in the whether-clause, and BSB repeats it.
The relative ᾧ ("to whom") is rendered to the one.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts the relative clause ᾧ ("to whom") as a when-clause, so ᾧ has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the recast relative clause with when.
English repeats the subject and copula in the whether-clause, which has no verb in Greek (as Galatians 4:7).

6:17.sourceText: χάρις δὲ τῷ Θεῷ ὅτι ἦτε δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὑπηκούσατε δὲ ἐκ καρδίας εἰς ὃν παρεδόθητε τύπον διδαχῆς,
6:17.targetText: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.

groups.note: The δέ ("but") of the obeyed clause is rendered by though in the first clause.
ἐκ καρδίας ("from the heart") is rendered wholeheartedly.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb in the Greek exclamation "thanks to God".
English adds an adverb marking the former state.

6:18.sourceText: ἐλευθερωθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐδουλώθητε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ.
6:18.targetText: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.

groups.note: The ending of ἐδουλώθητε ("you were enslaved") gives You, the subject of both verbs.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to the main verb with and; the Greek has no καί here.

6:19.sourceText: ἀνθρώπινον λέγω διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν. ὥσπερ γὰρ παρεστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνομίᾳ εἰς τὴν ἀνομίαν, οὕτως νῦν παραστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ εἰς ἁγιασμόν.
6:19.targetText: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.

groups.note: μέλη ("members") is rendered parts of … body.
δοῦλα ("as slaves") is rendered in slavery.
εἰς τὴν ἀνομίαν ("leading to lawlessness") is rendered escalating.
μέλη ("members") is rendered them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB leaves ὑμῶν ("your") untranslated with them.

6:20.sourceText: ὅτε γὰρ δοῦλοι ἦτε τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἐλεύθεροι ἦτε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ.
6:20.targetText: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.

groups.note: ἐλεύθεροι ("free") with the dative of respect is rendered free of obligation.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:21.sourceText: τίνα οὖν καρπὸν εἴχετε τότε; ἐφ’ οἷς νῦν ἐπαισχύνεσθε· τὸ γὰρ τέλος ἐκείνων θάνατος.
6:21.targetText: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.

groups.note: εἴχετε ("you had") is rendered did you reap with fruit.
ἐφ’ ("over, at") marks what one is ashamed of.
The relative οἷς ("which") is rendered with its implied antecedent, the things.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English links the fruit to its source with from.

6:22.sourceText: νυνὶ δέ ἐλευθερωθέντες ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δουλωθέντες δὲ τῷ Θεῷ, ἔχετε τὸν καρπὸν ὑμῶν εἰς ἁγιασμόν, τὸ δὲ τέλος ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
6:22.targetText: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.

groups.note: The participle ἐλευθερωθέντες ("having been set free") is rendered that … have been set free after now.
ἔχετε ("you have") is rendered you reap with fruit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ὑμῶν ("your") untranslated; the fruit you reap already makes it yours.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle ἐλευθερωθέντες ("having been set free").

6:23.sourceText: τὰ γὰρ ὀψώνια τῆς ἁμαρτίας θάνατος, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
6:23.targetText: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
